mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 3.0% signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Federal funds rate rose to 0.2% in March 2022, beginning a tightening cycle
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals tight labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy and suppress equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:UNRATE was 3.7% in March 2022, near pre-pandemic levels
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 3.5%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year window is below 0.03.
